title: Blood on the Tracks
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Middle schooler Seiichi Osabe lives with his doting mother, Seiko, until a shocking act on a family outing reveals her as possessive and unstable. The psychological horror follows Seiichi's warped relationship with her into adulthood (to verify).
life_message: A life of breaking free from a controlling bond to find one's own self.

content.note: A family member pushed from a cliff; later violence (to verify).

Sustained psychological horror: Seiko pushes her nephew off a cliff in front of her son Seiichi, then controls him through manipulation and distorted memories (Wikipedia); ComicsBeat calls it 'deeply unsettling', with the mother growing 'more unstable and intimately destructive'. Close-ups are deliberately disturbing.
Psychosexual mother-son tension is central (AniList Psychosexual 82%; ComicsBeat 'intimately destructive'). Exact depiction to verify.
Emotional abuse, bullying and suicide themes (AniList Suicide, Bullying signals) (to verify).

delivery.evidence: Ian Wolf (via Wikipedia) notes themes of maternal conflict and disturbing close-ups; nothing on preachiness (to verify).
delivery.note: The harm of a controlling mother is shown through Seiichi's experience rather than explained.

winners_losers: Seiko's control dominates and Seiichi suffers; no one wins cleanly. The story's sympathy lies with the child's struggle for selfhood.
to_verify: Fear and intensity raised 3 to 5 on 2026-11-22 (Wikipedia plus ComicsBeat). Mental health left at 3: neither source mentions suicide or self-harm, so the AniList Suicide tag is unconfirmed; both do confirm sustained psychological abuse by Seiko
